primitives.note: Orb of Deception and Charm deal their damage on a short (0.25s) cast/travel resolution and go back on cooldown; no other gating.

Orb of Deception is a returning projectile: it deals magic damage passing through the target outbound, then true damage passing back through it on return, i.e. two damage instances per cast against a stationary target.
Fox-Fire conjures three flames that land as separately timed hits on the same target if it is the only enemy champion present: one primary-damage hit and two subsequent (40%) hits.

Spirit Rush is castable up to 3 times within a 15s window (1s static cooldown between casts) at no extra mana cost, each cast firing bolts at up to 3 nearby visible enemies (only 1 relevant target vs a dummy).
Mana costs (Q 55-95, W 30, E 60, R 100) can meaningfully cap how many casts fit into the 15s window depending on mana pool/regen from items.

Essence Theft's stack-heal and takedown-heal only heal Ahri and never change damage dealt or taken by a stationary dummy; relevant only if Ahri herself is the survival-fight target and scores a kill/last-hit, which a single ongoing dummy fight will rarely realize mid-fight.

needsBespoke.why: All damage-relevant behavior (returning-projectile double hit on Q, multi-part delayed flame hits on W, free multi-cast structure on R, plain single-hit E, and self-only sustain on P) is expressible with the listed primitives.

unsettled.question: When does Fox-Fire's cooldown actually start: at cast, or only after the flames finish resolving (up to 2.5s later, per the wiki's 'starts post-effect' note)?
options: Cooldown starts at cast completion, like Q/E/R (treat cdstart as effectively on-cast for simulation purposes)
Cooldown starts only once all three flames have fired/expired, delaying the next W cast by up to ~2.5s beyond the listed cooldown value

unsettled.question: Against a single stationary target sitting at Orb of Deception's return point, does the 'return point circle' check add a distinct damage opportunity beyond the normal outbound-pass/return-pass hits, or is it fully subsumed by the 'each pass can only hit once' rule (i.e. no extra hit for a lone target)?
options: No extra hit: a lone target simply takes exactly one magic hit outbound and one true hit on return, as the two 'passes'
The return-point circle is a separate check that could, depending on exact geometry/timing, register as an additional instance distinct from the return pass
quotes: ''Orb of Deception'' will hit additional units around the return point in a small circle when the orb turns around.
This applies both to the initial and return missile's damage, but the initial missile only deals damage if the unit was not hit by it already.

unsettled.question: Charm's damage is stated to snapshot 'at the time of its application' (distinct wording from Q/W/R's 'current stats, changes dynamically'); does this mean the snapshot is taken at cast-completion (before travel) or at the moment of impact (after up to ~0.65s of travel at 1550 speed over up to 1000 range)?
options: Snapshot at cast completion (~0.25s after cast start), before the missile travels
Snapshot at impact, after travel time, functionally the same as the other spells' dynamic recalculation
quotes: This ability's damage is calculated based on the caster's stats at the time of its application.

proposal: Open the fight by casting Q (Orb of Deception) toward the dummy first since it is off cooldown and cheap relative to its long-cooldown counterparts.
Immediately follow with E (Charm) and W (Fox-Fire) in quick succession (all castable within roughly 1 second combined given their short/no cast times).

Cast R (Spirit Rush) once the initial Q/W/E volley is out, then immediately recast R twice more (1s apart) to spend all 3 free casts back-to-back early, since R's cooldown (100-140s) means it will not come off cooldown again inside the 15s window.
Fill all remaining time with basic attacks, and recast Q, E, and W each time they come off cooldown (Q every 7s, E every 12s, W every 5-9s depending on rank) for the rest of the 15 seconds.
Do not hold or delay any ability for setup purposes (no crowd-control sequencing needed against a stationary dummy); cast everything as soon as it is available and affordable.
questions: Does the simulator model Fox-Fire's 'starts post-effect' cooldown as delaying the next W cast, and if so by how long should that delay be assumed to be against a stationary target?

Should all three Spirit Rush casts be front-loaded at the very start of the fight, or is there a build/scenario where holding recasts later in the 15s window yields more total damage (e.g., to line up with cooldown resets on Q/W/E)?
Is mana assumed unlimited/fully regenerated for this rotation, or does the simulator enforce Ahri's actual mana pool and regen, which could force skipping casts of Q/E/R late in the 15s window?
Are basic attacks assumed to weave freely between every ability cast (i.e. cast times/animations don't block the attack timer), or do Q/E's 0.25s cast times delay the next auto-attack?
